limitations: effects depend on the task, delay, feedback, and question quality
it is not universally superior to every learning activity
retrieval_text: Study strategy: Retrieval practice with feedback. Attempt to recall or produce the target information before checking the answer. This supports durable learning for suitable recall and explanation tasks when questions and feedback are well matched. Practical use: answer before opening notes; check accuracy promptly; correct errors in complete form. Limits: effects depend on the task, delay, feedback, and question quality; it is not universally superior to every learning activity. Select this method only when it practises the target learning task, and use feedback where it is available.
title: Retrieval practice with feedback
unsuitable_use_cases: recognition-only review without an attempted answer
replacing practical performance with fact questions

implementation_guidance: schedule more than one opportunity when time permits
adapt spacing to the assessment horizon
limitations: optimal gaps vary with retention interval and material
the one-day planner can only begin a longer spacing schedule
retrieval_text: Study strategy: Spaced review across available opportunities. Revisit important material after a delay instead of placing every repetition in one block. The interval should reflect the retention goal and available plan rather than a single fixed rule. Practical use: schedule more than one opportunity when time permits; attempt retrieval on later reviews; adapt spacing to the assessment horizon. Limits: optimal gaps vary with retention interval and material; the one-day planner can only begin a longer spacing schedule. Select this method only when it practises the target learning task, and use feedback where it is available.
title: Spaced review across available opportunities
unsuitable_use_cases: claiming one interval is optimal for every learner
delaying urgent prerequisite learning beyond the available day

implementation_guidance: write or perform the corrected step
limitations: feedback quality and timing matter
some open-ended work requires a teacher, peer, or domain expert
retrieval_text: Study strategy: Prompt feedback and error correction. Check attempted work against an answer, test, rubric, example, or qualified feedback source, then correct the reasoning or performance rather than only marking it wrong. Practical use: complete an attempt first; locate the first meaningful error; write or perform the corrected step. Limits: feedback quality and timing matter; some open-ended work requires a teacher, peer, or domain expert. Select this method only when it practises the target learning task, and use feedback where it is available.
title: Prompt feedback and error correction
unsuitable_use_cases: copying an answer without comparing reasoning
using unreliable answer material

implementation_guidance: state why the step is allowed
check unclear explanations against a source
limitations: foundational evidence includes domain-specific studies
incorrect prior knowledge can produce incorrect explanations without feedback
retrieval_text: Study strategy: Self-explanation of examples and concepts. Explain why a step, relationship, or claim makes sense and connect it to prior knowledge. The explanation should expose gaps rather than paraphrase each line mechanically. Practical use: pause at meaningful steps; state why the step is allowed; check unclear explanations against a source. Limits: foundational evidence includes domain-specific studies; incorrect prior knowledge can produce incorrect explanations without feedback. Select this method only when it practises the target learning task, and use feedback where it is available.
title: Self-explanation of examples and concepts
unsuitable_use_cases: inventing explanations without checking accuracy
using explanation as a substitute for independent practice

implementation_guidance: choose an example matching the target problem type
cover the solution before the independent attempt
limitations: support should fade as competence grows
examples do not remove the need for varied independent practice
retrieval_text: Study strategy: Worked examples followed by independent problems. Study a relevant worked solution, explain its decisions, and then solve a related problem with progressively less support. Independent performance is the required final check. Practical use: choose an example matching the target problem type; cover the solution before the independent attempt; compare method selection and steps. Limits: support should fade as competence grows; examples do not remove the need for varied independent practice. Select this method only when it practises the target learning task, and use feedback where it is available.
title: Worked examples followed by independent problems
unsuitable_use_cases: copying several solved answers without attempting a problem
using an unrelated example

implementation_guidance: first identify the candidate problem types
explain the cue for each selected method
limitations: evidence is task- and domain-dependent
mixing can feel harder and must remain aligned to the goal
retrieval_text: Study strategy: Conditional interleaving of confusable problem types. Mix previously learned problem types when the learner must practise deciding which method applies. Keep initial instruction clear and avoid arbitrary switching among unrelated subjects. Practical use: first identify the candidate problem types; mix a small reviewed set; explain the cue for each selected method. Limits: evidence is task- and domain-dependent; mixing can feel harder and must remain aligned to the goal. Select this method only when it practises the target learning task, and use feedback where it is available.
title: Conditional interleaving of confusable problem types
unsuitable_use_cases: randomly alternating unrelated subjects
mixing unfamiliar types before basic instruction

implementation_guidance: mark only claims, evidence, or unclear terms
close the text and summarize a section
limitations: reading strategies must match the text and goal
annotation alone is not evidence of comprehension
retrieval_text: Study strategy: Purposeful reading with section summaries. Read with a question, identify claims and supporting evidence, and pause to summarize sections in the learner's own words. Selective annotation supports the purpose; marking every line does not. Practical use: write the reading question first; mark only claims, evidence, or unclear terms; close the text and summarize a section. Limits: reading strategies must match the text and goal; annotation alone is not evidence of comprehension. Select this method only when it practises the target learning task, and use feedback where it is available.
title: Purposeful reading with section summaries
unsuitable_use_cases: highlighting most of the page
reading without a follow-up explanation or response

implementation_guidance: create or inspect a contextual example
limitations: word knowledge includes form, meaning, and use
classroom vocabulary guidance requires adaptation for independent study
retrieval_text: Study strategy: Vocabulary meaning, context, and recall. Learn a word through a concise meaning, a meaningful example, and active recall in both directions. Revisit words and use them in reading, speaking, or writing context. Practical use: record a short accurate meaning; create or inspect a contextual example; retrieve meaning and production forms; check usage. Limits: word knowledge includes form, meaning, and use; classroom vocabulary guidance requires adaptation for independent study. Select this method only when it practises the target learning task, and use feedback where it is available.
title: Vocabulary meaning, context, and recall
unsuitable_use_cases: memorizing an inaccurate isolated translation
recognition-only card flipping

implementation_guidance: identify features rather than copy sentences
limitations: the main evidence guide targets secondary instruction
independent use requires an appropriate model and criteria
retrieval_text: Study strategy: Model, practice, and reflect for writing. Examine a relevant model, identify assignment features, draft a manageable section, and reflect and revise using criteria or feedback. The learner must produce original writing. Practical use: identify features rather than copy sentences; plan against task criteria; draft and revise a section. Limits: the main evidence guide targets secondary instruction; independent use requires an appropriate model and criteria. Select this method only when it practises the target learning task, and use feedback where it is available.
title: Model, practice, and reflect for writing
unsuitable_use_cases: copying a model response
spending the whole session reading advice

limitations: writing processes are recursive rather than rigid
available time may require one priority revision pass
retrieval_text: Study strategy: Plan, draft, and revise a written response. Separate planning, text production, and revision so that each stage has a concrete output. Revision should address meaning and organization before minor surface edits when the task permits. Practical use: translate the prompt into criteria; outline the claim and evidence; draft without copying; revise against the criteria. Limits: writing processes are recursive rather than rigid; available time may require one priority revision pass. Select this method only when it practises the target learning task, and use feedback where it is available.
title: Plan, draft, and revise a written response
unsuitable_use_cases: editing grammar before a main idea exists
treating the first draft as final

implementation_guidance: attempt questions without premature answer access
review both correct and incorrect reasoning
limitations: practice quality matters more than item count
transfer to substantially different tasks is not automatic
retrieval_text: Study strategy: Practice questions matched to the target performance. Use questions that require the same kind of recall, explanation, calculation, analysis, or production expected later. Vary surface features after the basic method is understood. Practical use: name the target performance; attempt questions without premature answer access; review both correct and incorrect reasoning. Limits: practice quality matters more than item count; transfer to substantially different tasks is not automatic. Select this method only when it practises the target learning task, and use feedback where it is available.
title: Practice questions matched to the target performance
unsuitable_use_cases: using fact questions for a performance-only skill
repeating one memorized item format

implementation_guidance: connect each part to the original problem
limitations: the best representation depends on the problem
school mathematics guidance should not be generalized to every university domain
retrieval_text: Study strategy: Connect visual and symbolic representations. Represent a problem or concept with an appropriate diagram, table, graph, model, or notation, then explain how the representations correspond. The visual must carry relevant meaning. Practical use: identify quantities and relationships; choose a meaningful representation; connect each part to the original problem. Limits: the best representation depends on the problem; school mathematics guidance should not be generalized to every university domain. Select this method only when it practises the target learning task, and use feedback where it is available.
title: Connect visual and symbolic representations
unsuitable_use_cases: adding decorative images
using an inaccurate diagram without checking it

implementation_guidance: state what is known and required
limitations: checking conventions vary by domain
a representation is useful only when it matches the relationships
retrieval_text: Study strategy: Represent, solve, and check a quantitative problem. Translate the situation into knowns, unknowns, constraints, and a representation before calculating. After solving, check units, plausibility, and consistency with the question when those checks apply. Practical use: state what is known and required; select a representation and method; solve and interpret the result. Limits: checking conventions vary by domain; a representation is useful only when it matches the relationships. Select this method only when it practises the target learning task, and use feedback where it is available.
title: Represent, solve, and check a quantitative problem
unsuitable_use_cases: calculating from keywords without modelling the situation
accepting an implausible answer without review

limitations: curriculum sources describe practices rather than causal study effects
tooling and language details vary
retrieval_text: Study strategy: Trace, build, and test small programs. Predict code behavior, trace important state, write a small program, run it, and use tests or examples to compare expected and actual behavior. Explain the result after execution. Practical use: predict before running; implement a small target behavior; test normal and boundary examples; explain discrepancies. Limits: curriculum sources describe practices rather than causal study effects; tooling and language details vary. Select this method only when it practises the target learning task, and use feedback where it is available.
title: Trace, build, and test small programs
unsuitable_use_cases: watching tutorials without producing code
copying a complete solution without testing understanding

implementation_guidance: record the failing input or action
limitations: some failures require tools or domain knowledge beyond a study session
the curriculum source is descriptive evidence
retrieval_text: Study strategy: Debug by reproducing, tracing, and testing a hypothesis. Make the failure reproducible, inspect the smallest relevant state, propose a cause, and test one controlled change. Finish by explaining the fault and adding a check when appropriate. Practical use: record the failing input or action; trace from observed behavior; change one relevant factor; rerun and explain. Limits: some failures require tools or domain knowledge beyond a study session; the curriculum source is descriptive evidence. Select this method only when it practises the target learning task, and use feedback where it is available.
title: Debug by reproducing, tracing, and testing a hypothesis
unsuitable_use_cases: making many unrelated edits at once
assuming the first suspected line is the cause

limitations: legal conventions differ by jurisdiction and course
the source defines educational outcomes rather than proving one study format
retrieval_text: Study strategy: Structured legal case analysis. Separate relevant facts, legal issues, authorities or rules, application, counterarguments, and a reasoned conclusion. Distinguish learning analysis from professional legal advice. Practical use: identify legally relevant facts; state the issue precisely; apply the assigned authorities; test an alternative argument. Limits: legal conventions differ by jurisdiction and course; the source defines educational outcomes rather than proving one study format. Select this method only when it practises the target learning task, and use feedback where it is available.
title: Structured legal case analysis
unsuitable_use_cases: giving personal legal advice
memorizing a case name without reasoning from its facts

implementation_guidance: label variables and units supplied by the source
describe the pattern before explaining it
limitations: methods depend on the scientific field and design
standards describe expected practices rather than one universal study method
retrieval_text: Study strategy: Interpret scientific data and limitations. Identify variables, patterns, uncertainty, and the claim a dataset can support. Compare the evidence with a model and state limitations without extending beyond the observations. Practical use: label variables and units supplied by the source; describe the pattern before explaining it; connect claims to specific evidence. Limits: methods depend on the scientific field and design; standards describe expected practices rather than one universal study method. Select this method only when it practises the target learning task, and use feedback where it is available.
title: Interpret scientific data and limitations
unsuitable_use_cases: inventing missing measurements
claiming causation from unsupported data

implementation_guidance: use only the approved procedure and safety guidance
limitations: laboratory safety is institution- and task-specific
this planner does not authorize or supervise experiments
retrieval_text: Study strategy: Pre-laboratory preparation and post-laboratory explanation. Before practical work, review the purpose, variables, approved procedure, and safety instructions. Afterward, organize observations and explain results and limitations using the course's required format. Practical use: use only the approved procedure and safety guidance; predict the expected relationship; prepare a data-recording structure; explain results afterward. Limits: laboratory safety is institution- and task-specific; this planner does not authorize or supervise experiments. Select this method only when it practises the target learning task, and use feedback where it is available.
title: Pre-laboratory preparation and post-laboratory explanation
unsuitable_use_cases: replacing required supervision or safety instruction
inventing procedures or hazards

implementation_guidance: compare at least two plausible alternatives
limitations: design constraints and testing standards are project-specific
professional safety review remains outside the planner
retrieval_text: Study strategy: Requirements, alternatives, prototype, and iteration. Translate a design brief into needs and constraints, generate more than one option, make a manageable prototype or representation, evaluate it against criteria, and record the next iteration. Practical use: write needs and constraints; compare at least two plausible alternatives; test against stated criteria; record trade-offs. Limits: design constraints and testing standards are project-specific; professional safety review remains outside the planner. Select this method only when it practises the target learning task, and use feedback where it is available.
title: Requirements, alternatives, prototype, and iteration
unsuitable_use_cases: selecting the first idea without criteria
claiming a prototype is validated without appropriate testing

implementation_guidance: explain the completed map without copying
limitations: evidence depends on implementation and comparison conditions
mapping does not replace practice of required procedures
retrieval_text: Study strategy: Concept mapping for organization and explanation. Create a concept map when relationships among ideas are the learning target. Label links, check the map against a source, and use it as a prompt for explanation or later recall. Practical use: select the central question; use concise concept nodes; label relationships; explain the completed map without copying. Limits: evidence depends on implementation and comparison conditions; mapping does not replace practice of required procedures. Select this method only when it practises the target learning task, and use feedback where it is available.
title: Concept mapping for organization and explanation
unsuitable_use_cases: decorative maps with unlabeled links
treating one comparison study as proof of universal inferiority

implementation_guidance: verify with a trusted course source
limitations: benefit depends on prior knowledge and answer accuracy
not every fact requires elaboration
retrieval_text: Study strategy: Elaborative why and how questions. Ask why a statement is true, how a process works, or when a principle applies, then check the explanation. Use questions that connect to the course material rather than unsupported speculation. Practical use: choose a central claim; answer from memory; verify with a trusted course source; revise inaccurate links. Limits: benefit depends on prior knowledge and answer accuracy; not every fact requires elaboration. Select this method only when it practises the target learning task, and use feedback where it is available.
title: Elaborative why and how questions
unsuitable_use_cases: accepting a plausible invented answer
using questions without checking them

implementation_guidance: state the corrected rule or action
limitations: cause labels may need teacher or expert feedback
recording errors is useful only when it changes later practice
retrieval_text: Study strategy: Error log focused on patterns and corrections. Record a small number of meaningful errors, their causes, corrected reasoning, and a future check. Group recurring error types so later practice targets the cause rather than repeating every item. Practical use: record the first meaningful error; state the corrected rule or action; schedule one related practice item. Limits: cause labels may need teacher or expert feedback; recording errors is useful only when it changes later practice. Select this method only when it practises the target learning task, and use feedback where it is available.
title: Error log focused on patterns and corrections
unsuitable_use_cases: copying every wrong answer without analysis
using the log as a punishment or score list

implementation_guidance: state why tasks are being mixed
limit the set to related material
limitations: interleaving evidence does not justify arbitrary subject switching
novices may need blocked introduction first
retrieval_text: Study strategy: Purposeful mixed practice without arbitrary task switching. Combine related tasks when the goal requires method selection or integration, while keeping each block long enough to complete an attempt and feedback cycle. Mixing is a design choice, not a rule for constant switching. Practical use: state why tasks are being mixed; limit the set to related material; complete and check each attempt. Limits: interleaving evidence does not justify arbitrary subject switching; novices may need blocked introduction first. Select this method only when it practises the target learning task, and use feedback where it is available.
title: Purposeful mixed practice without arbitrary task switching
unsuitable_use_cases: switching whenever work becomes difficult
mixing unrelated new material

implementation_guidance: attempt a short output without notes
compare it with evidence or criteria
limitations: a short check samples only part of learning
future planning must consider priority and available time
retrieval_text: Study strategy: End-of-session gap check and next step. Finish a session by attempting a brief explanation or performance, checking it, and naming one specific unresolved gap and next action. This makes progress visible without relying only on confidence. Practical use: attempt a short output without notes; compare it with evidence or criteria; write one concrete next step. Limits: a short check samples only part of learning; future planning must consider priority and available time. Select this method only when it practises the target learning task, and use feedback where it is available.
title: End-of-session gap check and next step
unsuitable_use_cases: rating confidence without checking performance
creating a long new task after the session ends
